svg.aria-label: How to write 停: 11 strokes · 10 pen lifts · 11 movements
svg.title: Writing 停
svg.desc: 11 frames; frame N shows movements 1 to N of 停 (chinese), the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished letter, whose outline is read from _fonts/NotoSansSC-Subset.ttf. Stroke order after Hanzi Writer Data 停.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–11 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chanind/hanzi-writer-data/68d10a4b21150cae5e1ebbd223eed289cf32d90c/data/%E5%81%9C.json>. Source note on variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies eleven ordered strokes for 停, in two pieces. Medians 1–2 draw 亻 as 他 opens: a left-falling stroke, then a vertical. Medians 3–11 draw the right side: a dot, a horizontal and 口, as 高 opens; the cover as 写 opens, a short left stroke and a horizontal that hooks down to the left without lifting; then a horizontal and a vertical down the middle that hooks to the left without lifting. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those eleven ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turns, the hook and ten intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.
svg.text: How it is written — 11 strokes · 10 pen lifts · 11 movements
